findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are embedded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and API to anyone with instance/describe permissions, leading to credential leakage.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, meaning data at rest on the volume is stored unencrypted and vulnerable to exposure if the underlying disk is compromised.
The EBS snapshot inherits from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, exposing data at rest in the snapshot to unauthorized access if shared or leaked.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from anywhere on the internet.
The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no other compensating controls (e.g., WAF), increasing exposed attack surface to the public internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of resources directly to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure of resources directly to the internet.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block/ACL restrictions defined, risking unauthorized access to or exposure of sensitive network log data.
